# 0010. Load dependency declarations by name, before resolution, into a shared layer

**Status:** Accepted **Date:** 2026-10-23

## Context

The pipeline parses only the project's own files, `@types/react` (full HTML-attribute mode) and TypeScript's lib files. An import into `node_modules` resolves to a path, but nothing parses that file, so a prop typed by a package (`ClosableType`, `OnValueChange`, a Radix primitive's props) stays an unresolved name. With dependencies installed, unresolved types sat at 116 (antd), 323 (chakra), 586 (spectrum) and about 1,000 (shadcn), and RDT expanded what we couldn't.

Loading whole files along imports is the wrong unit. The file-level closures of the five benchmark projects hold 150–6,218 files, and the cost is the file count: about 25 µs per file, almost all of it opening the file (18 threads open only 1.7× faster than one on macOS), against 418 MB/s for parsing. A prototype that loads only the files declaring a name the project uses read 39–833 files warm instead of 150–6,218.

## Decision

Behind `PipelineOptions::load_dependencies` (off by default), a phase before `NamedTypeIndex::build` loads the dependency declarations the project's type positions name, transitively, and nothing else.

- **Demands, not files.** A demand is a package specifier and an imported name used in a type position (a type reference, `typeof X`, heritage, a type argument). A loaded declaration's own references become new demands. One rayon scope runs them; each declaring file is claimed once, and results are keyed by file and name, so the outcome does not depend on scheduling.
- **A separate, shared layer.** Loaded declarations live in a `DependencyLayer` behind an `Arc`, with its own type index and import map. Project lookups fall back to it; keys are file paths, so the layers never collide. Watch revisions share it; an edit that adds a demand gets a new layer version with the new declarations added, never a copy of the project's data.
- **Precedence:** project declaration, then a known shortcut (`VariantProps`, `SxProps`, `HTMLChakraProps`, …), then a dependency declaration, then a builtin. The shortcuts exist because the real declarations are conditional types the structural resolver can't evaluate; a loaded declaration must not replace them.
- **Values stay out of the output.** A dependency's components go into a value index that `ComponentProps<typeof X>` and `typeof Pkg.Root` consult; they are never emitted. Dependency enums never become public output enums or feed the bare-name enum index.
- **Every unresolved demand is reported** on the component whose resolution reached it: a package with no types, an unresolvable specifier, a name the package doesn't export.

## Consequences

- In the experiment that proved this design (`exp/dependency-types`), unresolved types fell to 8 (mantine), 26 (chakra), 82 (shadcn), 58 (antd) and 172 (spectrum), for 2–29 ms of loading on a warm index.
- Props that reach large shared types grow sharply (chakra 560 → 398,910 in its own repo), which is why 0012 collapses large dependency sources and why resolved props are shared, not copied (#105).
- A watch edit that adds a package import costs one index lookup and a few files (under 1 ms in the prototype); `node_modules`, `package.json` and tsconfig changes still need `rebuild()`.
- `declare module` augmentations, `declare global` and `node:*` ambient modules are not loaded yet; a name only they provide stays unresolved, with a diagnostic.
- The TypeScript backend (0006, 0007) gets fewer incomplete components to handle; both now report parents inside `node_modules`.

# 0010. Load dependency declarations by name, before resolution, into a shared layer

**Status:** Accepted **Date:** 2026-10-23

## Context

The pipeline parses only the project's own files, `@types/react` (full HTML-attribute mode) and TypeScript's lib files. An import into `node_modules` resolves to a path, but nothing parses that file, so a prop typed by a package (`ClosableType`, `OnValueChange`, a Radix primitive's props) stays an unresolved name. With dependencies installed, unresolved types sat at 116 (antd), 323 (chakra), 586 (spectrum) and about 1,000 (shadcn), and RDT expanded what we couldn't.

Loading whole files along imports is the wrong unit. The file-level closures of the five benchmark projects hold 150–6,218 files, and the cost is the file count: about 25 µs per file, almost all of it opening the file (18 threads open only 1.7× faster than one on macOS), against 418 MB/s for parsing. A prototype that loads only the files declaring a name the project uses read 39–833 files warm instead of 150–6,218.

## Decision

Behind `PipelineOptions::load_dependencies` (off by default), a phase before `NamedTypeIndex::build` loads the dependency declarations the project's type positions name, transitively, and nothing else.

- **Demands, not files.** A demand is a package specifier and an imported name used in a type position (a type reference, `typeof X`, heritage, a type argument). A loaded declaration's own references become new demands. One rayon scope runs them; each declaring file is claimed once, and results are keyed by file and name, so the outcome does not depend on scheduling.
- **A separate, shared layer.** Loaded declarations live in a `DependencyLayer` behind an `Arc`, with its own type index and import map. Project lookups fall back to it; keys are file paths, so the layers never collide. Watch revisions share it; an edit that adds a demand gets a new layer version with the new declarations added, never a copy of the project's data.
- **Precedence:** project declaration, then a known shortcut (`VariantProps`, `SxProps`, `HTMLChakraProps`, …), then a dependency declaration, then a builtin. The shortcuts exist because the real declarations are conditional types the structural resolver can't evaluate; a loaded declaration must not replace them.
- **Values stay out of the output.** A dependency's components go into a value index that `ComponentProps<typeof X>` and `typeof Pkg.Root` consult; they are never emitted. Dependency enums never become public output enums or feed the bare-name enum index.
- **Every unresolved demand is reported** on the component whose resolution reached it: a package with no types, an unresolvable specifier, a name the package doesn't export.

## Consequences

- In the experiment that proved this design (`exp/dependency-types`), unresolved types fell to 8 (mantine), 26 (chakra), 82 (shadcn), 58 (antd) and 172 (spectrum), for 2–29 ms of loading on a warm index.
- Props that reach large shared types grow sharply (chakra 560 → 398,910 in its own repo), which is why 0012 collapses large dependency sources and why resolved props are shared, not copied (#105).
- A watch edit that adds a package import costs one index lookup and a few files (under 1 ms in the prototype); `node_modules`, `package.json` and tsconfig changes still need `rebuild()`.
- `declare module` augmentations, `declare global` and `node:*` ambient modules are not loaded yet; a name only they provide stays unresolved, with a diagnostic.
- The TypeScript backend (0006, 0007) gets fewer incomplete components to handle; both now report parents inside `node_modules`.

Yes, Homebrew uses Ruby for its formula DSL. I’d **keep Bash and the existing Python scripts in caliper**. The parity and equivalence scripts are already wired into CI and do substantial JSON analysis; rewriting them in Ruby would add churn without closing a prop gap or resolving a conflict.

I resolved the conflicts in #201 and #202; every open PR now reports as mergeable, and #202’s Equivalence check passed. I also opened [#221](https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper/pull/221) to fix the crate dependency metadata that stopped the 0.6.0 release, and added a regression test. Its code checks pass; Changesets remains red because that earlier release left `caliper-docgen@0.6.0` unpublished. I have not published any crates.

name: Release & Publish

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      release_source_sha:
        description: 'Merged Callisto release-PR commit to recover; leave empty for the triggering commit.'
        required: false
        type: string

# Registry credentials exist only inside `execute`.
permissions: {}

# Per-commit group: a shared group would drop a queued release merge.
concurrency:
  group: release-${{ github.sha }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always
  # Keep in lockstep with .prototools.
  RUST_VERSION: "1.98.1"

jobs:
  release-candidate:
    name: Identify a merged Callisto release PR
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    timeout-minutes: 10
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: read
    outputs:
      is_release_pr: ${{ steps.candidate.outputs.is_release_pr }}
      release_source_sha: ${{ steps.candidate.outputs.release_source_sha }}
    steps:
      - id: candidate
        shell: bash
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          RELEASE_SOURCE_SHA_INPUT: ${{ inputs.release_source_sha }}
          TRIGGERING_SHA: ${{ github.sha }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          release_source_sha="${RELEASE_SOURCE_SHA_INPUT:-$TRIGGERING_SHA}"
          if [[ ! "$release_source_sha" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ ]]; then
            echo "::error::release_source_sha must be exactly 40 lowercase hex characters"
            exit 1
          fi
          resolved_sha=$(gh api "/repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/commits/${release_source_sha}" --jq '.sha')
          if [[ "$resolved_sha" != "$release_source_sha" ]]; then
            echo "::error::release_source_sha does not resolve to that exact commit"
            exit 1
          fi
          # Scheduling hint only; `callisto release plan` is the authority.
          prs=$(gh api --paginate "/repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/commits/${release_source_sha}/pulls" \
            --jq '[.[] | select(.merged_at != null and .base.ref == "main" and .head.repo.full_name == "'"${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"'" and (.head.ref == "callisto/version-packages" or (.head.ref | test("^callisto/version-packages--[0-9a-f]{40}$"))))] | length')
          verified=$(gh api "/repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/commits/${release_source_sha}" --jq '.commit.verification.verified')
          if [[ "$prs" == 1 && "$verified" == true ]]; then
            {
              echo 'is_release_pr=true'
              echo "release_source_sha=$release_source_sha"
            } >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo 'is_release_pr=false' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  version-pr:
    name: Create or update the Callisto release PR
    needs: release-candidate
    if: >-
      needs.release-candidate.outputs.is_release_pr != 'true' &&
      inputs.release_source_sha == ''
    timeout-minutes: 15
    concurrency:
      group: version-pr
      cancel-in-progress: false
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write
      pull-requests: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      # Pinned here, not inherited from the action's default.
      - uses: orin-dx/callisto/.github/actions/setup-callisto@c3d524d3aba359f5e767007ea76d229e8a291dc3 # callisto@0.12.0
        with:
          version: callisto@0.12.0
          verification: require
      - name: Compose, version, and open the release PR
        uses: orin-dx/callisto/.github/actions/callisto-action@c3d524d3aba359f5e767007ea76d229e8a291dc3 # callisto@0.12.0
        with:
          setup_callisto: 'false'
          branch: main
          release_branch: callisto/version-packages
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}

  plan:
    name: Derive release intent from the merged release commit
    needs: release-candidate
    if: needs.release-candidate.outputs.is_release_pr == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 20
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: orin-dx/callisto/.github/actions/setup-callisto@c3d524d3aba359f5e767007ea76d229e8a291dc3 # callisto@0.12.0
        with:
          version: callisto@0.12.0
          verification: require
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.release_source_sha }}
          path: release-source
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Derive and hash intent
        env:
          RELEASE_SOURCE_SHA: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.release_source_sha }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          handoff_dir="${RUNNER_TEMP}/release-intent"
          mkdir -p "$handoff_dir"
          callisto release plan \
            --source-root "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/release-source" \
            --orchestration-revision "$GITHUB_SHA" \
            --from-release-commit "$RELEASE_SOURCE_SHA" \
            --decision "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/release-source/.callisto/release-decision.json" \
            --out "$handoff_dir/release-intent.json"
          shasum -a 256 "$handoff_dir/release-intent.json" > "$handoff_dir/release-intent.json.sha256"
      # No `[release]` section here, so callisto-managed artifact slots are unexpected.
      - name: Reject unexpected artifact slots
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [[ "$(jq '.artifactSlots | length' "${RUNNER_TEMP}/release-intent/release-intent.json")" != "0" ]]; then
            echo "::error::intent declares artifact slots but this workflow has no build job"
            exit 1
          fi
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: release-intent
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-intent
          if-no-files-found: error
          # Long enough to re-run `execute` after a multi-day diagnosis.
          retention-days: 7

  build:
    name: Build ${{ matrix.platform }}
    needs: [release-candidate, plan]
    timeout-minutes: 45
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.host }}

{"baseRefName":"main","body":"## Summary

- Make the TypeScript transport and semantic backend publishable crates and give every dependency in the published CLI's local crate chain a registry version requirement.
- Add both crates to Callisto's crates.io release graph and record the package-boundary decision in ADR 0021.

The [0.6.0 release run](https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper/actions/runs/40261575594) published `caliper-docgen-core`, then Cargo rejected the CLI manifest because `caliper-docgen-semantic` had only a path dependency and was marked unpublishable. The semantic crate also depended on an unpublishable transport crate.

## Verification

- `cargo package -p caliper-docgen-tsc-client --allow-dirty --no-verify` packages 26 files.
- `cargo package -p caliper-docgen-semantic --allow-dirty --list` lists its package contents.
- `cargo test -p caliper-docgen-semantic -p caliper-docgen-tsc-client` passes.
- `cargo check -p caliper-docgen` passes.
- `git diff --cached --check` passed before commit.

`cargo package` for the semantic crate cannot resolve `caliper-docgen-tsc-client` from crates.io until the transport crate is published. Callisto's dependency graph must publish transport, semantic, then CLI. No registry publication is part of this PR.

## Release follow-up

The failed 0.6.0 release source is immutable and its CLI package was not published. A new release plan containing this fix is needed; rerunning that old source cannot repair its manifest. Existing Changesets preflight failures on #201 and #202 report that the CLI's current 0.6.0 version is absent from crates.io.

name: Release & Publish

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      release_source_sha:
        description: 'Merged Callisto release-PR commit to recover; leave empty for the triggering commit.'
        required: false
        type: string

# Registry credentials exist only inside `execute`.
permissions: {}

# Per-commit group: a shared group would drop a queued release merge.
concurrency:
  group: release-${{ github.sha }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always
  # Keep in lockstep with .prototools.
  RUST_VERSION: "1.98.1"

jobs:
  release-candidate:
    name: Identify a merged Callisto release PR
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    timeout-minutes: 10
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: read
    outputs:
      is_release_pr: ${{ steps.candidate.outputs.is_release_pr }}
      release_source_sha: ${{ steps.candidate.outputs.release_source_sha }}
    steps:
      - id: candidate
        shell: bash
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          RELEASE_SOURCE_SHA_INPUT: ${{ inputs.release_source_sha }}
          TRIGGERING_SHA: ${{ github.sha }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          release_source_sha="${RELEASE_SOURCE_SHA_INPUT:-$TRIGGERING_SHA}"
          if [[ ! "$release_source_sha" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ ]]; then
            echo "::error::release_source_sha must be exactly 40 lowercase hex characters"
            exit 1
          fi
          resolved_sha=$(gh api "/repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/commits/${release_source_sha}" --jq '.sha')
          if [[ "$resolved_sha" != "$release_source_sha" ]]; then
            echo "::error::release_source_sha does not resolve to that exact commit"
            exit 1
          fi
          # Scheduling hint only; `callisto release plan` is the authority.
          prs=$(gh api --paginate "/repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/commits/${release_source_sha}/pulls" \
            --jq '[.[] | select(.merged_at != null and .base.ref == "main" and .head.repo.full_name == "'"${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"'" and (.head.ref == "callisto/version-packages" or (.head.ref | test("^callisto/version-packages--[0-9a-f]{40}$"))))] | length')
          verified=$(gh api "/repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/commits/${release_source_sha}" --jq '.commit.verification.verified')
          if [[ "$prs" == 1 && "$verified" == true ]]; then
            {
              echo 'is_release_pr=true'
              echo "release_source_sha=$release_source_sha"
            } >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo 'is_release_pr=false' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  version-pr:
    name: Create or update the Callisto release PR
    needs: release-candidate
    if: >-
      needs.release-candidate.outputs.is_release_pr != 'true' &&
      inputs.release_source_sha == ''
    timeout-minutes: 15
    concurrency:
      group: version-pr
      cancel-in-progress: false
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write
      pull-requests: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      # Pinned here, not inherited from the action's default.
      - uses: orin-dx/callisto/.github/actions/setup-callisto@c3d524d3aba359f5e767007ea76d229e8a291dc3 # callisto@0.12.0
        with:
          version: callisto@0.12.0
          verification: require
      - name: Compose, version, and open the release PR
        uses: orin-dx/callisto/.github/actions/callisto-action@c3d524d3aba359f5e767007ea76d229e8a291dc3 # callisto@0.12.0
        with:
          setup_callisto: 'false'
          branch: main
          release_branch: callisto/version-packages
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}

  plan:
    name: Derive release intent from the merged release commit
    needs: release-candidate
    if: needs.release-candidate.outputs.is_release_pr == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 20
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: orin-dx/callisto/.github/actions/setup-callisto@c3d524d3aba359f5e767007ea76d229e8a291dc3 # callisto@0.12.0
        with:
          version: callisto@0.12.0
          verification: require
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.release_source_sha }}
          path: release-source
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Derive and hash intent
        env:
          RELEASE_SOURCE_SHA: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.release_source_sha }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          handoff_dir="${RUNNER_TEMP}/release-intent"
          mkdir -p "$handoff_dir"
          callisto release plan \
            --source-root "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/release-source" \
            --orchestration-revision "$GITHUB_SHA" \
            --from-release-commit "$RELEASE_SOURCE_SHA" \
            --decision "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/release-source/.callisto/release-decision.json" \
            --out "$handoff_dir/release-intent.json"
          shasum -a 256 "$handoff_dir/release-intent.json" > "$handoff_dir/release-intent.json.sha256"
      # No `[release]` section here, so callisto-managed artifact slots are unexpected.
      - name: Reject unexpected artifact slots
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [[ "$(jq '.artifactSlots | length' "${RUNNER_TEMP}/release-intent/release-intent.json")" != "0" ]]; then
            echo "::error::intent declares artifact slots but this workflow has no build job"
            exit 1
          fi
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: release-intent
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-intent
          if-no-files-found: error
          # Long enough to re-run `execute` after a multi-day diagnosis.
          retention-days: 7

  build:
    name: Build ${{ matrix.platform }}
    needs: [release-candidate, plan]
    timeout-minutes: 45
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.host }}

# 0007. Let the backend discover components, always compile it in, and keep structural as the default

**Status:** Accepted **Date:** 2026-10-21

## Context

ADR 0006 made the TypeScript backend a second resolver that finishes components the structural resolver already found. Detection by shape now covers 92 to 99% of the components react-docgen-typescript (RDT) reports on five large libraries (`docs/edge-cases.md`), and what is left is a call with no type argument (`lazy()`, `createIconLoader("x")`) or a prop a callee adds (Mantine's `component` and `renderRoot` on 220 components). Only the checker can answer those: it knows what the call returns. Separately, callisto's rule is no cargo features in shipped crates, which ADR 0006's "feature-gated crate" contradicts.

## Decision

- **Discovery.** The backend may add components the structural pass did not find, using RDT's rule: a declaration whose type has a call signature with a props-shaped first parameter. Each carries the rule that found it and merges into the structural output; on a clash the structural entry wins.
- **Always compiled, enabled at runtime.** `crates/tsc-client` is a normal dependency of the CLI and the NAPI addon, with no cargo feature. A runtime option turns it on and is off by default, so a run without it spawns nothing.
- **Structural stays the default and the fallback.** A missing, unsupported or crashing `tsc` leaves the structural result untouched and adds a diagnostic.
- **Trigger.** The backend runs only for components the structural pass marked incomplete (an opaque leaf, a wrapper call with no resolved props, a callee-added prop it cannot see) plus whole-project discovery when the option asks for it. It is never a silent default.
- **Output.** `ExtractionOutput` gains an additive `schemaVersion` so consumers can tell whether discovery was on. Existing fields keep their shape.

## Consequences

- Wrapper calls the structural pass cannot see become exact without a new heuristic per library.
- Every build pays for the client's dependencies. Users who never enable the backend pay nothing at runtime.
- The checker needs `typescript` 7.1 or later and sees a dependency edit only when told. `WatchSession::update_file` must notify it, with a parity test against `extract()`.
- Checker types do not fit `PropType` losslessly, so a checker answer is converted at the boundary and anything that does not fit stays opaque with a reason.
- Determinism needs a gate: a clean run and an incremental run must agree, measured on the five corpora with dependencies installed.
- Supersedes only the feature-gating bullet of ADR 0006. The rest of 0006 stands.

## Alternatives considered

- **Keep the backend a feature of a separate crate.** Matches ADR 0006 as written but breaks the no-features rule and makes the shipped binary vary by build.
- **Run it by default.** Costs a process per run on projects that structural detection already handles and makes output depend on a toolchain being installed.
- **Add one structural heuristic per remaining shape.** The remaining shapes need the callee's return type; a heuristic per library is what the shape-based detector was built to avoid.

To depend on a library hosted on crates.io, add it to your `Cargo.toml`.

    `

You’re right to challenge it. **#221 is not necessary for the prop-gap work, and I should not have opened a publish-two-crates PR as the default fix.** I marked it **draft** so it won’t be merged as proposed.

I opened it because the 0.6.0 release failed: the CLI depends on the semantic crate by local path, and [Cargo requires a registry version for dependencies of a published crate](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/specifying-dependencies.html#local-paths-in-published-crates). Publishing both internal crates is one solution, but it expands our public release surface and #221 still does not repair the partially published 0.6.0 release or its red Changesets checks.

My recommendation is to park #221 and return to the gap work. The Cargo release needs a separate decision: keep `cargo install` by publishing those dependencies or consolidating them into the CLI, or stop publishing the CLI to crates.io. I made that architecture choice prematurely.

## Installing from NPM

Caliper is published as the @hyperledger/caliper-cli NPM package, providing a single point of install for every supported adapter.

### Versioning semantics

Before explaining the steps for installing Caliper, let’s take a look at the versions page of the CLI package. You will see a list of tags and versions. If you are new to NPM, think of versions as immutable pointers to a specific version (duh) of the source code, while tags are mutable pointers to a specific version. So tags can change where they point to. Easy, right?

But why is all this important to you? Because Caliper is still in its pre-release life-cycle (< v1.0.0), meaning that even minor version bumps are allowed to introduce breaking changes. And if you use Caliper in your project, you might run into some surprises depending on how you install Caliper from time to time.

# Releasing

How a Callisto-managed release moves from changeset to published package.

For registry credential setup (npm, crates.io, PyPI), see [`publishing.md`](publishing.md).

---

## Local release: `callisto release`

`callisto release` selects packages without a tag for their current version. It publishes to registries, creates tags and GitHub releases, and records HEAD as the source. It can run on any branch.

- `callisto release --dry-run` prints the plan and performs no effect. It works anywhere, including on a dirty worktree or without an `origin` remote (tags are then noted as unbound).
- `--package <ecosystem/name>` (repeatable) restricts the run to named unreleased packages, all distributions of each (naming `npm/dual` also releases `cargo/dual`), plus every member of their fixed or linked groups. An unreleased workspace package that a selected one depends on (runtime, optional, or peer) must be selected too.
- It refuses a dirty worktree: a tracked modification or an untracked file not covered by `.gitignore`. Ignored files never count.
- It prints `Nothing to release.` and exits 0 when every package is already tagged.
- It prints a summary. With `--receipt <file>` it also writes the receipt there, only when every selected operation succeeded. An existing tag can exclude unfinished work before those operations are selected; see the retry limit below.
- A workspace with artifact slots or napi platform packages must release through CI. See the generated workflow below.

`cargo`, `npm`, `twine`, and `gh` report their own authentication failures. With the original release intent, the executor can adopt matching completed effects.

### Current retry limit

If a local release tags a version but fails before pushing the tag or completing GitHub work, a fresh `callisto release` at the same commit lists the package again, observes each remaining effect and finishes it.

- `Nothing to release.` is not proof of completion for a tag on an older commit: the retry looks only at tags on the commit being released.
- Generated simple workflows share this limit.
- CI releases based on the merged release PR retain the original package list.

---

## Generated workflows

`callisto init --workflow` (or answering yes to its prompt) writes `.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml`. Keep that filename for generated artifact releases.

Init never overwrites an existing file. This repo's [release workflow](../.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml) is a worked example.

- **Simple shape** (no artifact slots or napi platform packages): `version-pr` maintains the release PR. On each default-branch push, `release` runs `callisto release`; it is a no-op until an untagged version is merged.
- **Build-matrix shape** (artifact slots or napi platform packages): a release PR, then plan -> build -> publish. The build covers configured targets and artifact slots.
- Maturin builds, and platform packages without `napi.targets`, get no generated workflow.

Generated actions configure npm and Twine authentication during execution. Manual workflows must configure native authentication as described in [publishing.md](publishing.md).

Generated build support has these boundaries:

- Cargo `bin` targets can become GitHub release assets. npm `bin` and Python `[project.scripts]` are registry releases, not artifact products (E304).
- Co-located Cargo/Maturin manifests fail discovery with E007.
- Custom artifact builders need `--no-workflow` and a manual workflow that fills every configured artifact slot.
- Registry-only npm and PyPI releases need no artifact slots.

The default branch is the approval boundary: a merge to it publishes. Protect it with a rule that requires pull requests and reviews (GitHub -> Settings -> Rules). Init prints this reminder after writing the file.

Pin the Callisto actions by commit with the version in a comment, such as `uses: orin-dx/callisto/.github/actions/callisto-action@<sha> # callisto@1.0.0`. The action installs the release that commit belongs to. From 1.0.0 the floating tag `v1` also works (`@v1`): each stable 1.x release moves it to its release commit, never backwards, and the action installs that release. A mutable tag is only as safe as the repository that moves it, so a pinned commit stays the stricter choice.

Build-matrix limits:

- An addon crate outside the napi package directory needs a unique crate whose lib name matches `napi.binaryName` (E204).
- Generated `.node` files must be gitignored; release execution requires a clean checkout.
- Cargo `bin` targets build with `cargo build --release --locked`. Other products, such as `cdylib`s, need a manual workflow.
- The napi build and placement roster comes from the release intent, so an unrelated addon does not block a release of another package.
- Native npm lifecycle hooks run unchanged, including any owner-defined publishing or forge effects. Those effects are outside Callisto's release graph.

---

## Release PR and approval

The generated workflow keeps a release PR current. Merging that PR to the protected default branch authorizes publication; Callisto adds no approval step. Require reviews and CI checks in branch protection. A CODEOWNERS file alone does not enforce review.

The action's `version-pr` mode updates the PR; `release` runs `callisto release` for simple workspaces. Artifact and platform packages use plan/build/execute. See the [action inputs](../.github/actions/callisto-action/action.yml).

Only `execute` receives registry credentials. Keep `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN`, `NPM_TOKEN`, and `TWINE_PASSWORD` out of workflow scope, planning and build jobs, and action inputs.

After a failed committed-decision CI release, "Re-run failed jobs" adopts completed effects and performs the rest. A green workflow alone is not proof of publication: check the receipt and providers.

## PR pre-flight verification

[`.github/actions/callisto-validate/action.yml`](../.github/actions/callisto-validate/action.yml) is a reusable action for your PR workflow:

- `callisto status --check` — one gate covering config health, package discovery, and changeset syntax: exit 0 with no error-level diagnostics, exit 1 otherwise.
- `callisto release --dry-run --format text` — simulates the release plan without effect.
- Writes a workspace status summary to the job's GitHub Actions summary page.

---

## Release identity and recovery

Every release run records two different revisions:

- The **orchestration revision**: the workflow and Callisto CLI that coordinate the run.
- The **release-source revision**: the merged release commit whose exact versions are released.

A recovery is a new run using current orchestration and an explicit full release-source SHA. It does not rerun historical workflow code, create a version PR, or invent a newer version.

To retry a failed run for the same source, use "Re-run failed jobs". Matching completed effects are adopted; conflicting or uncertain results stop the run. A receipt is written only after every selected operation succeeds.

Callisto waits for a published version to appear before it announces anything: up to 6 minutes for npm and PyPI, 2 for Cargo. npm packages are published back to back and waited for together, so a release of many npm packages waits once, not once per package; Cargo and PyPI publishes are waited for as they are published. If the registry is slower it stops with E157; re-run the failed job once the version shows, or set `confirm-timeout` on the registry in `callisto.toml` (see [configuration](config.md#registries)) and keep the job's `timeout-minutes` above the total wait.

## Recovering an older release

Recovering a commit that is no longer a branch tip may require these manual actions:

**E180: the workflow can't push tags.** GitHub rejects a `GITHUB_TOKEN` tag push when the tagged commit's workflows differ from every branch tip. Push every tag of the release yourself (PAT or deploy key), then dispatch the release for that SHA:

```sh
SHA=<release-source sha>
git tag -a "<tag>" -m "Release <tag>" "$SHA"   # each tag of the release
git push origin "<tag>"
gh workflow run callisto-release.yml --ref main -f release_source_sha="$SHA"
```

**`ArtifactAssetDiffers`: rebuilt assets don't match.** Rebuilt tarballs aren't byte-identical. Delete the mismatched assets and dispatch again:

```sh
gh release delete-asset "<release tag>" "<asset>" --yes   # each mismatched asset
gh workflow run callisto-release.yml --ref main -f release_source_sha="$SHA"
```

## Publication checks

Callisto checks the registry, remote tag, and GitHub release before each effect. An exact match is adopted; a conflict or uncertain result stops the run. Check the receipt and providers before treating a release as complete.

Registry checks confirm version presence, not identical bytes or the npm dist-tag. A Python release is complete only when every built wheel and sdist is on the index; a partly uploaded one is finished by uploading the missing files, and a sealed build also compares each file's digest. See [publishing limits](publishing.md#current-python-support-limits).

GitHub Releases start as drafts. Assets upload before the release is made public.

- It refuses a dirty worktree: a tracked modification or an untracked file not covered by `.gitignore`. Ignored files never count.
- It prints `Nothing to release.` and exits 0 when every package is already tagged.
- It prints a summary. With `--receipt <file>` it also writes the receipt there, only when every selected operation succeeded. An existing tag can exclude unfinished work before those operations are selected; see the retry limit below.
- A workspace with artifact slots or napi platform packages must release through CI. See the generated workflow below.

`cargo`, `npm`, `twine`, and `gh` report their own authentication failures. With the original release intent, the executor can adopt matching completed effects.

### Current retry limit

If a local release tags a version but fails before pushing the tag or completing GitHub work, a fresh `callisto release` at the same commit lists the package again, observes each remaining effect and finishes it.

- `Nothing to release.` is not proof of completion for a tag on an older commit: the retry looks only at tags on the commit being released.
- Generated simple workflows share this limit.
- CI releases based on the merged release PR retain the original package list.

---

## Generated workflows

`callisto init --workflow` (or answering yes to its prompt) writes `.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml`. Keep that filename for generated artifact releases.

Init never overwrites an existing file. This repo's [release workflow](../.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml) is a worked example.

- **Simple shape** (no artifact slots or napi platform packages): `version-pr` maintains the release PR. On each default-branch push, `release` runs `callisto release`; it is a no-op until an untagged version is merged.
- **Build-matrix shape** (artifact slots or napi platform packages): a release PR, then plan -> build -> publish. The build covers configured targets and artifact slots.
- Maturin builds, and platform packages without `napi.targets`, get no generated workflow.

Generated actions configure npm and Twine authentication during execution. Manual workflows must configure native authentication as described in [publishing.md](publishing.md).

Generated build support has these boundaries:

- Cargo `bin` targets can become GitHub release assets. npm `bin` and Python `[project.scripts]` are registry releases, not artifact products (E304).
- Co-located Cargo/Maturin manifests fail discovery with E007.
- Custom artifact builders need `--no-workflow` and a manual workflow that fills every configured artifact slot.
- Registry-only npm and PyPI releases need no artifact slots.

The default branch is the approval boundary: a merge to it publishes. Protect it with a rule that requires pull requests and reviews (GitHub -> Settings -> Rules). Init prints this reminder after writing the file.

Pin the Callisto actions by commit with the version in a comment, such as `uses: orin-dx/callisto/.github/actions/callisto-action@<sha> # callisto@1.0.0`. The action installs the release that commit belongs to. From 1.0.0 the floating tag `v1` also works (`@v1`): each stable 1.x release moves it to its release commit, never backwards, and the action installs that release. A mutable tag is only as safe as the repository that moves it, so a pinned commit stays the stricter choice.

Build-matrix limits:

- An addon crate outside the napi package directory needs a unique crate whose lib name matches `napi.binaryName` (E204).
- Generated `.node` files must be gitignored; release execution requires a clean checkout.
- Cargo `bin` targets build with `cargo build --release --locked`. Other products, such as `cdylib`s, need a manual workflow.
- The napi build and placement roster comes from the release intent, so an unrelated addon does not block a release of another package.
- Native npm lifecycle hooks run unchanged, including any owner-defined publishing or forge effects. Those effects are outside Callisto's release graph.

---

## Release PR and approval

The generated workflow keeps a release PR current. Merging that PR to the protected default branch authorizes publication; Callisto adds no approval step. Require reviews and CI checks in branch protection. A CODEOWNERS file alone does not enforce review.

The action's `version-pr` mode updates the PR; `release` runs `callisto release` for simple workspaces. Artifact and platform packages use plan/build/execute. See the [action inputs](../.github/actions/callisto-action/action.yml).

Only `execute` receives registry credentials. Keep `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN`, `NPM_TOKEN`, and `TWINE_PASSWORD` out of workflow scope, planning and build jobs, and action inputs.

After a failed committed-decision CI release, "Re-run failed jobs" adopts completed effects and performs the rest. A green workflow alone is not proof of publication: check the receipt and providers.

## PR pre-flight verification

[`.github/actions/callisto-validate/action.yml`](../.github/actions/callisto-validate/action.yml) is a reusable action for your PR workflow:

- `callisto status --check` — one gate covering config health, package discovery, and changeset syntax: exit 0 with no error-level diagnostics, exit 1 otherwise.
- `callisto release --dry-run --format text` — simulates the release plan without effect.
- Writes a workspace status summary to the job's GitHub Actions summary page.

---

## Release identity and recovery

Every release run records two different revisions:

- The **orchestration revision**: the workflow and Callisto CLI that coordinate the run.
- The **release-source revision**: the merged release commit whose exact versions are released.

A recovery is a new run using current orchestration and an explicit full release-source SHA. It does not rerun historical workflow code, create a version PR, or invent a newer version.

To retry a failed run for the same source, use "Re-run failed jobs". Matching completed effects are adopted; conflicting or uncertain results stop the run. A receipt is written only after every selected operation succeeds.

Callisto waits for a published version to appear before it announces anything: up to 6 minutes for npm and PyPI, 2 for Cargo. npm packages are published back to back and waited for together, so a release of many npm packages waits once, not once per package; Cargo and PyPI publishes are waited for as they are published. If the registry is slower it stops with E157; re-run the failed job once the version shows, or set `confirm-timeout` on the registry in `callisto.toml` (see [configuration](config.md#registries)) and keep the job's `timeout-minutes` above the total wait.

## Recovering an older release

Recovering a commit that is no longer a branch tip may require these manual actions:

**E180: the workflow can't push tags.** GitHub rejects a `GITHUB_TOKEN` tag push when the tagged commit's workflows differ from every branch tip. Push every tag of the release yourself (PAT or deploy key), then dispatch the release for that SHA:

```sh
SHA=<release-source sha>
git tag -a "<tag>" -m "Release <tag>" "$SHA"   # each tag of the release
git push origin "<tag>"
gh workflow run callisto-release.yml --ref main -f release_source_sha="$SHA"
```

**`ArtifactAssetDiffers`: rebuilt assets don't match.** Rebuilt tarballs aren't byte-identical. Delete the mismatched assets and dispatch again:

```sh
gh release delete-asset "<release tag>" "<asset>" --yes   # each mismatched asset
gh workflow run callisto-release.yml --ref main -f release_source_sha="$SHA"
```

## Publication checks

Callisto checks the registry, remote tag, and GitHub release before each effect. An exact match is adopted; a conflict or uncertain result stops the run. Check the receipt and providers before treating a release as complete.

Registry checks confirm version presence, not identical bytes or the npm dist-tag. A Python release is complete only when every built wheel and sdist is on the index; a partly uploaded one is finished by uploading the missing files, and a sealed build also compares each file's digest. See [publishing limits](publishing.md#current-python-support-limits).

GitHub Releases start as drafts. Assets upload before the release is made public.

# Architecture Decision Records

Short, dated records of _architectural_ decisions — ones that shape system structure, boundaries, or contracts other code depends on. Not a changelog, not a design doc, not a place to explain what the code does — comments and `ARCHITECTURE.md` already do that.

## Index

One line per ADR, with what it guards. Add a line when you add an ADR.

- [1. Parse with OXC instead of the TypeScript compiler](0001-oxc-over-typescript-compiler.md) — do not add a type-checking pass to the default path. The opt-in backend is 0006.
- [2. Hand-write Serialize/Deserialize for PropType instead of deriving it](0002-manual-serialize-for-prop-type.md) — do not derive them on `PropType` or `CollectedType`.
- [3. Cache the DTS parse cache with positional (not named) MessagePack](0003-positional-msgpack-cache-encoding.md) — do not reorder, insert or remove `SourceData` fields without bumping `CACHE_SCHEMA_VERSION`.
- [4. Defer full type-checker integration](0004-defer-type-checker-integration.md) — superseded by 0006.
- [5. Contain panics at a single, per-item boundary](0005-panic-containment-boundary.md) — route anything reachable from a rayon `.map()`, a `DocgenPlugin` hook or a NAPI entry point through `contain_panic`.
- [6. Run the TypeScript backend as a second resolver](0006-semantic-backend-as-second-resolver.md) — do not patch `Opaque` leaves, give `crates/core` a compiler process or I/O, or route the backend through NAPI.

- [7. Let the backend discover components, always compile it in, and keep structural as the default](0007-backend-discovers-components-and-compiles-in.md) — do not feature-gate the backend crate, run it by default, or let it replace a structural entry on a clash.
- [8. Discard the parse cache whenever the build that wrote it differs](0008-parse-cache-keyed-by-build.md) — do not load cache entries without checking the payload's header against the running build.
- [9. Write each distinct prop once in the canonical output](0009-canonical-output-interns-props.md) — do not inline props in canonical JSON or derive prop ids from position.
- [10. Load dependency declarations by name, before resolution, into a shared layer](0010-load-dependency-declarations-by-name.md) — do not load dependency files by import closure, resolve against them lazily during resolution, or emit their components or enums. Its precedence of shortcuts over dependency declarations is superseded by 0014.
- [11. Find dependency declarations through a per-package export index, not the parse cache](0011-per-package-export-index.md) — do not put dependency files in the `DtsCache` or reuse an index whose package's `package.json` changed.
- [12. Collapse large inherited dependency sources, as Storybook does](0012-collapse-large-dependency-sources.md) — do not resolve a collapsed source's props, or collapse a component's own props.
- [13. Read React's attribute declarations in curated mode, in an index of their own](0013-curated-mode-reads-react-attributes-apart.md) — do not merge React into the project index outside Full mode, or make the React index a lookup fallback.
- [14. A loaded declaration wins over a known shortcut; shortcuts are fallbacks](0014-declarations-before-shortcuts.md) — do not check a shortcut before a declaration, or add one without measuring it against the declaration on consumer code.
- [15. A member read through React's types reads React's declaration and what it imports](0015-member-reads-of-react-types-read-their-declarations.md) — do not answer an indexed access from a table before its declaration, or add React's own files to the dependency layer. Narrows 0013's "only HTML-attribute lookups read the React index" and 0010's "the loader doesn't read React".
- [16. Resolve components on request, and load dependencies for the names their resolution reaches](0016-resolve-components-on-request.md) — do not make a lazy answer differ from batch extraction's for the same key, memoize a resolution that found a dependency name missing, or expose a parser type from the session API. Extends 0010's loading from "before resolution" to "before the resolution that answers".
- [17. Version the canonical JSON, and make readers reject a version they don't read](0017-version-the-canonical-json.md) — do not change the canonical JSON's shape without bumping `SCHEMA_VERSION`, or let a reader accept a version it was not written for.
- [18. Write prop sets and name lists once in the canonical output](0018-canonical-output-interns-prop-sets-and-name-lists.md) — do not write a component's props, an inheritance layer's `omitted` or a diagnostic's `affects` inline in canonical JSON. Extends 0009's per-prop table to the lists that repeat across components; `SCHEMA_VERSION` 2.
- [20. Chain dependency layers and load the remaining names after three growths](0020-chain-dependency-layers.md) — keep dependency growth incremental and bound lookup depth. Supersedes 0016's 48-growth threshold.

Changing any of these needs a new ADR.

## When to write one

Two gates, both required:

1. **Architectural.** It affects one of: system structure (module/crate boundaries, how components interact), a dependency or technology choice that ripples across the codebase, a data format or contract other code depends on, or a cross-cutting constraint (performance model, correctness discipline, security model).
2. **Expensive to reverse and not obvious from the code.** If it gets reverted in a year, what breaks, and would anyone know why?

If either answer is no, it's not an ADR.

Good candidates:

- Choosing OXC over the TypeScript compiler — a technology choice that shapes the whole extraction pipeline
- A serialization format with a hidden constraint (msgpack's positional encoding) — a data contract other code depends on
- Dropping a dependency, or an approach that was tried and abandoned

Not ADR material:

- A single function's algorithm choice, confined to that function — that's a code comment
- A bug fix — commit message, and if it's the kind of thing that could recur, a line in `rdt-coverage.md`
- A behavior-preserving refactor — commit message is enough
- A naming or style convention — that's `AGENTS.md` or a lint rule
- Anything already obvious from the code or from `AGENTS.md`'s non-negotiables
- Per-user preferences, workflow notes and tool quirks — that's agent memory

## Format

One file per decision: `docs/adr/NNNN-short-title.md`, numbered sequentially, never reused. Copy `0000-template.md` to start.

- **Never edit history.** If a decision changes, write a new ADR and mark the old one's status `Superseded by 000X`. Don't rewrite the old file to look like you knew all along.
- **Status** is one of: `Accepted`, `Superseded by NNNN`, `Deprecated`.
- Keep it short. If the technical depth doesn't fit on a screen, split it into its own doc and link it — see `0006-semantic-backend-as-second-resolver.md` pointing at `type-checker-integration.md` instead of inlining it.

## Writing it

Write like you're explaining it to the next engineer over their shoulder, not presenting it to a committee. Don't hard-wrap paragraphs at a fixed column — one line per paragraph, let the editor soft-wrap. Every other doc in this repo already does this; hard-wrapping just makes future diffs noisy when a sentence gets edited.

**Cut the filler.** If a sentence still means the same thing without a word, delete the word.

| Instead of | Write |
| --- | --- |
| "It's worth noting that this decision was made in order to leverage OXC's robust parsing capabilities" | "OXC parses in parallel with no type-checking pass" |
| "This represents a significant improvement in performance" | "32ms instead of several seconds" |
| "We decided to essentially utilize a positional encoding approach" | "We use positional encoding" |
| "In conclusion, this architecture provides a solid foundation going forward" | (delete — you already said the thing) |

**Banned by default:** _leverage, utilize, robust, seamless, cutting-edge, essentially, basically, in order to, it's worth noting, it is important to note, at the end of the day._ If one is genuinely the precise technical word for something, fine — but check first.

**Concrete beats vague.** Name the file, the number, the benchmark. "Slow" is not a fact; "several seconds on a mid-size design system" is.

**Active voice, plain structure.** "We chose X because Y" beats "X was chosen due to Y considerations." Sentence-case headers, not Title Case.

**Show the trade-off, not just the win.** A decision with no downside isn't a decision, it's a fact. Say what it costs.

**Structure isn't fixed.** A paragraph, a paragraph plus bullets, a short table — whatever makes it scannable in one pass. `0006`'s Decision section is an intro line plus three bullets because it's three real choices; don't force that into one paragraph, and don't add sections or padding a one-line decision doesn't need.

## What good looks like

Read `0002-manual-serialize-for-prop-type.md` — a real bug behind it, a real number (`recursion_limit = 2048`), a real consequence, four sections, no throat-clearing.

---
name: changeset
description: Classify verified changes and produce one changeset per independent consumer-facing topic. Use when the user asks to add a changeset, document a change, or determine release impact.
---

State material concerns, evidence, consequence, and confidence directly. Do not soften blockers, manufacture praise, or claim certainty beyond the evidence.

# Record release intent at authoring time

Read the actual diff and any available implementation evidence before writing a changeset. A changeset is the durable consumer-facing statement that release aggregation consumes later; do not re-derive its intent from a vague summary.

## Workflow

1. Inspect the diff and group files by independent product or API topic.
2. Read `shared/references/delivery/changesets.md` before choosing `consumer_impact` or `semver_impact`.
3. For each topic, connect changed behavior to the linked requirement, spec, plan, or exact criteria evidence when available.
4. Produce one object per topic conforming to `shared/schemas/changeset@2.json`.
5. Validate required fields, especially `files_changed` and `acceptance_criteria_met`, against observed evidence.

## Classification rules

- Use `internal-only` only when a consumer cannot observe any behavior, API, configuration, or operational change.
- Use the largest required semver impact for the topic; do not dilute a breaking change because it is bundled with a smaller feature.
- Preserve uncertainty in `reasoning`; do not invent evidence or line numbers.

# Changesets

## Outcome

Record one coherent consumer-facing change in `changeset@2` so release tooling can preserve its meaning and calculate semver without reinterpreting prose. See `shared/schemas/changeset@2.json`.

## Consumer impact

| Value | Use when |
| :--- | :--- |
| `behavior-change` | Existing observable behavior changes for a consumer |
| `new-capability` | A consumer can do something new |
| `internal-only` | No behavior changes outside the repository |

`release-summarizer` omits `internal-only` entries from consumer release notes.

## Topic boundary

Use one changeset per independently releasable topic. Use these signals in priority order:

1. A shared linked requirement, spec, or plan defines one scope.
2. The author explicitly identifies a coordinated delivery scope.
3. The live diff shows one part exists because of another.

Do not split one outcome by package or file count. Do not bundle changes that could ship independently merely because they share a branch. When the boundary remains uncertain, state the ambiguity in `reasoning` and prefer the split that preserves accurate impact classification.

Verify `consumer_impact`, `semver_impact`, changed files, tests, and criteria evidence against that topic's own diff slice.

## Semver

| Change | Impact |
| :--- | :--- |
| Documentation or self-description only | `none` |
| Internal refactor or test-only change | `none` |
| Bug fix in runtime agent or skill behavior | `patch` |
| New optional schema field | `minor` |
| New schema or skill | `minor` |
| New plugin | `minor` |
| Removed or renamed schema field | `major`; create a new schema version |
| Renamed plugin ID or incompatible consumer behavior | `major` |

The release version is the highest `semver_impact` among included changesets. Classification comes from the structured field, not wording intensity.

## Breaking changes

Each breaking entry states:

- Old behavior.
- New behavior.
- Required consumer action.

Do not call an internal implementation change breaking unless it changes a supported consumer contract.

## Voice

Lead with observable consumer impact. Include a reason only when it changes understanding or action. Omit internal agent, file, and implementation detail unless the consumer must know it. State limitations and migration work directly. Full standard: `shared/references/authoring/voice.md`.

## Changeset, commit, and release note

| Artifact | Reader | Focus |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Commit | Maintainer reading history | Technical outcome and non-obvious reason |
| Changeset | Package consumer and release tooling | Observable impact and semver |
| Release note | Consumer deciding whether or how to upgrade | Grouped impact and required action |

Write a changeset when a PR changes runtime behavior, adds a consumer capability, changes a model or effort tier, changes a shared schema, adds a skill or plugin, or changes a verification protocol. Skip documentation, reference-only, internal refactor, and test-only changes unless they alter runtime instructions consumed by an agent.

## Release shape

```markdown
## v2.0.0 (2026-08-04)

### Breaking Changes
- Old behavior → new behavior. Required action.

### New Features
- Consumer-visible capability.

### Bug Fixes
- Corrected consumer-visible behavior.
```
